methodologyNotes: Ten current high-search gaming headsets spanning budget to flagship tiers (2022-2024 release years), independently re-verified against official manufacturer product pages and newsroom press releases (SteelSeries/GN, Razer, HyperX/HP, Logitech G, Corsair) plus reputable reviews (Tom's Hardware, TechRadar, SoundGuys, PC Gamer, RTINGS). Driver sizes in mm, weights in grams. battery_hours = manufacturer headline wireless figure (RGB off where two figures exist; null for wired). surround_sound and rgb are presence booleans. Adversarial fact-check (2026-06-15) corrected two values: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 priceUsd 149->179.99 (draft's $149/$199 narrative was fabricated; $199 is the Gen 2 price, $179.99 is the original launch MSRP) and Corsair HS80 Max weight_g 352->360 (official Corsair spec page lists 0.36 kg). All ten products verified to exist; all source URLs resolve and are topical. accessedAt 2026-06-15.

products.name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless
products.priceNote: MSRP at launch; current street price varies ~$250-310
products.provenance: Verified: SteelSeries product page confirms 40 mm neodymium (custom Hi-Fi) drivers, two-battery Infinity Power System rated up to 22 hours per battery, and retractable AI noise-cancelling (ClearCast Gen 2) mic. MSRP $349 and weight 338 g corroborated by Tom's Hardware and TechRadar. No RGB on this model. Source URL confirmed live and topical.

products.name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7 Wireless
products.priceNote: Launch MSRP (corrected from draft's $149; $199 figure cited in draft is the separate Nova 7 Gen 2 price)
products.provenance: CORRECTED priceUsd 149->179.99. The draft's claim that current MSRP is $149 (originally $199, 'reduced with Gen 2 release') is fabricated: the Arctis Nova 7 Wireless launched at $179.99 (TechRadar review, Amazon, SoundGuys all confirm $179.99/$180); the $199 figure belongs to the later Arctis Nova 7 Gen 2. Driver 40 mm neodymium, 326 g weight, 38-hour 2.4 GHz battery, retractable ClearCast Gen 2 mic and spatial-audio surround confirmed via Amazon spec listing and reviews. Release Aug 22, 2022 confirmed via GN Group press release (URL live). No RGB. Note: SteelSeries product-page URL currently surfaces the 7P variant landing, but the Nova 7 (non-P) is the same family and specs match; kept as primary source.

products.name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 1
products.provenance: Verified via Tom's Hardware and retailers: $60 MSRP, 236 g weight, 40 mm custom Hi-Fi (neodymium) driver, wired 3.5 mm, fully retractable mic, 360 spatial-audio surround. Battery null (wired-only). Released 2022 alongside Nova 3 and Nova 7.

products.name: HyperX Cloud III
products.provenance: Verified: HP newsroom press release (URL live) confirms announcement May 30, 2023 at COMPUTEX, $99.99 MSRP, 53 mm angled drivers, detachable 10 mm boom mic, DTS Headphone:X surround. Weight 308 g (320 g with mic) confirmed by Amazon spec listing and reviews. Battery null (wired-only). No RGB.

products.name: HyperX Cloud III Wireless
products.provenance: Verified: announced at Gamescom Aug 23, 2023; $169.99 MSRP, 53 mm angled drivers, up to 120-hour battery, detachable 10 mm boom mic, DTS Headphone:X surround. Weight 330 g (342 g with mic) per reviews. Amazon corroboration URL (ASIN B0CBQXGZ85) confirmed live and topical. No RGB.

products.priceNote: MSRP; Razer page currently shows $169.99 (15% off)

products.name: Razer Kraken V4
products.provenance: Verified directly from Razer product page: 40 mm TriForce Titanium driver, 350 g, retractable HyperClear Super Wideband mic, THX Spatial Audio, $179.99 MSRP, Razer Chroma 9-zone RGB. products.name: Logitech G Pro X 2 Lightspeed
products.provenance: Verified: Logitech IR press release (URL live) confirms May 24, 2023 launch, $249 USD MSRP, 50 mm PRO-G Graphene driver. 50-hour battery, detachable boom mic, DTS Headphone:X 2.0 surround, and 345 g weight confirmed by Amazon listing and Tom's Hardware. No RGB (deliberate pro aesthetic).

products.name: Astro A50 X Lightspeed
products.provenance: Verified: Logitech press release (URL live) confirms announced Dec 5, 2023, shipped first half of 2024, $379.99 MSRP. 40 mm PRO-G Graphene driver, 24-hour battery, integrated flip boom mic, Dolby Atmos surround confirmed via Logitech G product page and reviews. Weight 363 g confirmed by reviewers. No RGB (status LEDs only). releaseDate kept as 2024 (ship year).

products.name: Corsair HS80 Max Wireless
products.priceNote: MSRP (confirmed on official Corsair page; some retailers list ~$179.99)
products.provenance: CORRECTED weight_g 352->360. Official Corsair product page lists 0.36 kg (360 g); the draft's 352 g was a review-derived rounding. All other specs verified on the Corsair page: 50 mm neodymium driver, $189.99 MSRP, flip-to-mute omni-directional boom mic, Dolby Atmos surround, iCUE RGB on the logo, battery up to 65 hours (2.4 GHz, RGB off) / 24 hours (RGB on) / 130 hours (Bluetooth).
